reasoning: Recent state-specific public polling on Michigan’s 2026 Senate race shows a narrow Republican edge overall, with the latest polling average at R+1.9. The race is also now past the Democratic primary, and the available sources in the last 45 days are mostly primary polls rather than general-election head-to-head polling, so the best current statewide general-election signal in the supplied results is the polling average from aggregated Senate data.

sources.name: PollsMax Michigan Senate Polling Average
sources.details: Weighted polling average for the Michigan Senate race shows 45.1% Republican to 43.1% Democratic, giving Rogers a R+1.9 margin.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling / WLNS / WOODTV
sources.details: Emerson College/WLNS/WOODTV survey of likely Democratic primary voters found Abdul El-Sayed leading Haley Stevens 54% to 39% in the Michigan Senate Democratic primary.

sources.name: WLNS 6 News
sources.details: Coverage of the Emerson College/WLNS/WOODTV Democratic primary poll reported El-Sayed ahead of Stevens 54% to 39%.

sources.name: Detroit News / WDIV-TV / Glengariff Group
sources.details: Detroit News/WDIV-TV poll of likely Democratic primary voters found Haley Stevens leading Abdul El-Sayed 48.2% to 41.4%.

sources.name: The New York Times / Tulchin Research (via quoted poll topline)
sources.details: A Tulchin Research poll discussed in the New York Times showed El-Sayed ahead of Stevens in the Democratic primary, part of a series of primary polls in late July.
